<x_0.0205><y_0.2156>2. The cryftals of this falt are in the form of fine Propers prifms. It has a bitter, acrid, and ammoniacal tafte. <x_0.0225><y_0.2977>When it is rapidly heated, it inflames fpontaneoufly. <x_0.2559><y_0.5109>8. Muriate of Magneña.<x_0.6611><y_0.5281><class_Section-header>

<x_0.0234><y_0.5297>1. This compound of muriatic acid and magneña was formerly called _marine falt of magneña_, and was convounded with the muriate of lime, with which it is frequently accompanied. The difference between thefe two falts was firft pointed out by Dr Black, and Bergman afterwards examined the nature and properties of muriate of magneña. The falt is obtained by differing magneña in muriatic acid till they are fatu- rated, and then evaporating the folution. Small irregu- lar cryftals are obtained. This falt exits in the waters of the ocean, and in mineral waters, along with the mu- riates of foda and lime.<x_0.9756><y_0.6953><class_Text>

<x_0.0264><y_0.6945>2. It is extremely difficult to obtain the muriate of Properti magneña in any regular form. It is either in the fate of powder, or very fmall regular needles, or in a kind of jelly. It has a difagreeable bitter tafte. The fpe- cific gravity is 1.601.<x_0.9785><y_0.7641><class_Text>

<x_0.0322><y_0.7633>3. It is very deliquefect in the air. Cold water readily diffolves its own weight, and it is fill more fo- luble in boiling water.<x_0.8965><y_0.8055><class_Text>

<x_0.0332><y_0.8039>4. It is completely decompofed by heat ; the acid is driven off, and the pure earth remains behind ?.<x_0.9824><y_0.8336><class_Text>
